root.name: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation Accepted
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. d4 exd4

overview: White opens the centre and the usual line is 5.Nxd4 Bb4 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Bd3 d5 8.exd5 cxd5 9.O-O O-O 10.Bg5 c6 11.Qf3. White has active pieces and a small initiative, Black has a sound but slightly passive position with the bishop pair gone and a damaged queenside. Black can also play 5...Bc5 or 5...Nxd4 for different structures.

white_ideas.idea: Trade on c6 to damage Black's pawn structure, then develop with Bd3 and O-O.
Pin the knight with Bg5 and use the initiative.

black_ideas.idea: Hit the centre with ...d5 and trade pieces to simplify.
Use the half-open b-file and the bishop pair to counter.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after ...d5 and exd5 with Black's doubled c-pawns turned into c6 and d5.

character.notes: Open, active play but fewer early risks. Balanced.

gambit.notes: The d4 pawn comes straight back.

structure.notes: Pawns come off in the centre early; open lines for the pieces.

level.notes: Intermediate; plans are easy to see.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...Bc5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. d4 exd4 5. Nxd4 Bc5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black accepts a worse structure for activity.

character.reason: Active but not forcing; Black is safe.

gambit.reason: The d4 pawn is recaptured at once.

structure.reason: Open lines for the pieces early, as in the Scotch.

plans.reason: White's activity plays against Black's damaged queenside.
